text: Which statement about the decidability and complexity of propositional logic is correct?
choices: Propositional validity is undecidable, just like first-order validity
Propositional logic is decidable (truth tables always terminate), and Cook proved SAT is NP-complete
SAT is known to be solvable in polynomial time
explanation: Truth tables give a terminating decision procedure, so propositional logic is decidable, and Cook (1971) proved that SAT (CNF satisfiability) is NP-complete. It is first-order logic — not propositional logic — that is only semi-decidable (options 1 and 4). Whether SAT ∈ P is the open P = NP question, so option 3 is not known.
